title: Why Airplane Windows Have a Tiny Hole
lines: Look closely at an airplane window. There's a tiny hole in it.
It's not a defect. It's called a breather hole.
Because an airplane window actually has three layers.
The outer pane is the one that holds back the cabin pressure.
The tiny hole lets air through the middle pane, so only the outer pane takes the load.
If the outer pane ever cracks, the middle one is ready to take over.
And the hole lets moisture escape, so your window doesn't fog up.
That tiny hole is there to keep you safe. Follow for more!
caption:
That tiny hole in airplane windows is on purpose ✈️ Windows have 3 layers. The breather hole in the middle pane balances the pressure, so the outer pane carries the load and the middle pane stays ready as a backup. It also stops the window from fogging up.
